factProposals.value: The exact source text behind every summary is archived in Redis under relay:source:<sha256> for 30 days, and checked against its hash when read back.
The review queue now carries two kinds of entry: low_confidence classifications (STORY-007) and ungrounded_summary rejections (STORY-012).

decisions.statement: The summarizer is only ever called after source data has been fetched, found non-empty and archived.
decisions.rationale: a summarizer given nothing (or something unrecorded) fills the gap from its own knowledge; REQ-016 needs every summary traceable to the exact text it came from.

decisions.statement: If the source can't be archived, the summary fails instead of being produced without a record.
decisions.rationale: an unverifiable summary is exactly what the trust criterion rules out; failing is visible and retryable.

decisions.statement: Ungrounded summaries go to the review queue with the rejected text, violations and source reference, and are never returned as results.
decisions.rationale: the grounding guardrail's own caller contract: a rejection routes to review, never to silent persistence.

limitations.statement: The grounding check is lexical (word overlap and numbers). A summary that reuses the source's words but changes their meaning can pass.
No real LLM summarizer or source fetcher is wired in; both are injected functions, and the demo uses scripted stand-ins.
